Optimal Tuning Parameter by Information Criteria

Source: R/aic_relax.R
aic.islasso.Rd

Selects the tuning parameter `lambda` of an [islasso()] model by minimising an information criterion (AIC, BIC/eBIC, AICc, GCV or GIC; see [islasso.path()] for the definitions), as an alternative to cross-validation.

Usage

aic.islasso(
  object,
  method = c("AIC", "BIC", "AICc", "GCV", "GIC"),
  interval,
  g = 0,
  y,
  X,
  intercept = FALSE,
  family = gaussian(),
  alpha = 1,
  offset,
  weights,
  unpenalized,
  control = is.control(),
  trace = TRUE
)

Arguments

object

a fitted model of class `"islasso"` (optional if `y` and `X` are given).

method

the criterion to minimise.

interval

the search interval for `lambda`; by default the range of the glmnet path used to obtain the starting values of `object`.

g

numeric in \[0, 1\]: the parameter of the extended BIC (`g = 0` gives the BIC).

y, X

response and model matrix (without the column of ones), used if `object` is missing.

intercept, family, alpha, offset, weights, unpenalized, control

as in [islasso.fit()], used if `object` is missing.

trace

logical: print the progress of the optimisation?

Value

The value of `lambda` minimising the criterion.

Details

The criterion is minimised over \(\log\lambda\) with [stats::optimize()]; the degrees of freedom are the effective number of parameters (trace of the pseudo hat matrix).

See also

[islasso()], [islasso.path()], [GoF.islasso.path()]

Author

Gianluca Sottile gianluca.sottile@unipa.it

Examples

# \donttest{
n <- 100; p <- 30
beta <- c(rep(1, 5), rep(0, p - 5))
sim1 <- simulXy(n = n, p = p, beta = beta, seed = 1, family = gaussian())
o <- islasso(y ~ ., data = sim1$data, family = gaussian(), lambda = 5)
lambda.bic <- aic.islasso(o, method = "BIC", interval = c(1, 50), trace = FALSE)
o2 <- update(o, lambda = lambda.bic)
# }
